// diagnostic

E2307

A declared string view would outlive a possible owning `String`, has no stable public owner set, or `copies: .Explicit` forbids the owning materialization needed at a non-view destination.

What

A declared string view would outlive a possible owning `String`, has no stable public owner set, or `copies: .Explicit` forbids the owning materialization needed at a non-view destination.

Why

`View<str>` follows the same inferred owner-set rule as `View<T>` through calls, aggregates, callbacks, and trait contracts. Local and temporary owners still die too soon; an owned `String` still cannot fill a declared `View<str>` slot.

Fix

Keep every possible owner alive, use a proven `View<str>` boundary, write `~view` at the highlighted owning expression (the checker grades that edit), or remove `copies: .Explicit` for the default owning copy.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E2307: tests/ui/core_string_view_reuse_after_json.stderr.

Error [E2307]: `view` cannot be used directly here without an owning copy
  --> tests/ui/core_string_view_reuse_after_json.jet:7:23
    |
  7 |     node :: JSON.Text(view)
    |                       ^^^^
 Why: `view` is a zero-copy view into `raw` (`.trim()`/`.after()`/`.before()`); this destination needs an owned `String`, and `copies: .Explicit` keeps the implicit materialization disabled
 Fix: Write `~view` first, or remove `copies: .Explicit` to use the default owning copy
